_comment: The NESTED submission layout, and the only fixture that has one: --sca-root is the archive, the add-on code sits in addon/ and the Experiment implementation under addon/experiment/. Every other SCA fixture is FLAT - the add-on code sits at the archive root - so a file is keyed identically in the archive and against the add-on, and such a fixture cannot tell the two apart or reach any path arithmetic that runs against a non-empty add-on root. This one holds both side by side, so a drift between them shows up as a golden diff. Every path here is the SUBMISSION's: the review corpus IS --sca-root, so a reported path is the one the reviewer finds in the archive they were given. The add-on root is applied where a DECLARATION is read instead - the VENDOR entry below says `lib/widget.js` and resolves to addon/lib/widget.js. What it pins: the source's own manifest is read from addon/, so its __MSG_extName__ name resolves against addon/_locales and no localization finding fires; main.js is reviewed, which its fake namespace reports; the VENDOR file is found at the ADD-ON's own root - not wherever the submission keys it - and its declaration `lib/widget.js` is read relative to the ADD-ON, not the archive - offline nothing verifies, so applyUnverifiedVendor reconciles it into the untrusted family and unsafe-html reads the file as authored code; the --sca-exp-source exclusion keeps core-symbol-in-webext silent on the privileged ChromeUtils call (drop the flag and it reports experiment/exp.js, which is what makes the exclusion load-bearing here rather than incidental) - while unsafe-html still reports the innerHTML sink in that same file, because the exclusion is scoped to the WebExtension API/permission checks and a file is still reviewed for WHAT IT IS (privileged code shipped with a sink, minified or obfuscated is worse, not exempt); build.js sits beside the add-on's code rather than inside it, and is reviewed all the same - its own fake namespace is reported, because the whole archive is the review source: a build may move or generate anything, so no subtree can be called the add-on's. package.json and its lock are at the archive root where they belong, so the build checks stay silent and the build-review escalation anchors there - the one archive-relative path in the report.
